title: Change Visibility Ledger & Escrowed Approval — PRD (sketch)
body:
Purpose
This sketch proposes a 'Change Visibility Ledger' (CVL) plus an 'Escrowed Approval' mechanism for customer-managed networking changes in Private deployments. Goal: make every configuration or operator-initiated change (customer or Redwood-side) provably visible, auditable, and safely revertible while minimizing operational friction for customers who want local control over networking.

Problem statement
- Customers deploying Redwood Private often manage their own VPCs/network appliances. Change events (route updates, firewall rules, peering, BGP policies, NAT changes) are source-of-truth in customer systems — Redwood needs a reconciled, tamper-evident view to:
  - support forensics when requests fail or model endpoints degrade,
  - meet audit / compliance requirements for evidence of approvals,
  - enable safe automated rollbacks and emergency operator workflows.
- Existing PRDs in this folder focus on approval gates and logs separately. We need a single lightweight object model and APIs for: (1) recording change evidence, (2) express approval state (requested, staged, escrowed, approved, rejected, revoked), and (3) attaching machine-verifiable artifacts (signed config snapshots, telemetry, pcap pointers).

Scope
- Index of change events for customer-managed networking relevant to Private deployments (VPC peering, route tables, firewall/NSG rules, NAT, VPN tunnels, IP allowlist changes).
- Escrowed Approval flow for high-risk changes: ability to hold a change pending customer attestation or operator signoff.
- Audit evidence bundles (immutable metadata + pointers to artifacts stored in customer S3/KMS or Redwood vault depending on customer policy).
- Retention tiers and configurable sampling for telemetry (full vs sampled packet traces).
- APIs and console surface in Redwood Console for visibility and investigation.
- Basic rollback orchestration hooks (does not implement full change orchestration).

Non-goals
- Replace customer's own CMDB or infra-as-code.
- Full automated remediation for arbitrary network changes.
- Re-architecting control-plane security (this sits on top of existing Private control plane auth).

User personas
- Customer platform engineer: wants evidence that a change was accepted, and to produce it for their auditors.
- Redwood SRE/Support: needs quick access to change timeline and artifacts when handling incidents.
- Security/compliance reviewer: needs tamper-evident approval trails for attestation.
- Solutions engineer during onboarding: wants to validate customer acceptance windows and test rollback flows.

High-level design
1) Change Visibility Ledger (CVL) object model
   - change_id: UUID (ledger primary key)
   - actor: {type: customer/operator, identity string}
   - target: {resource_type: route/table/firewall/vpn, resource_id}
   - delta: short natural language summary + structured diff (text)
   - evidence_refs: list of signed artifact pointers (S3 URI, Redwood vault blob id)
   - approval_state: requested | staged | escrowed | approved | rejected | revoked
   - escrow_expiry: optional timestamp for auto-release/auto-reject
   - related_incident_ids: list of incident ids
   - immutable_hash: hash over canonicalized record (for tamper evidence)

   Records are append-only. Mutations create new ledger entries pointing to previous change_id (linked-list) and update approval_state immutably (i.e., new ledger entry with state transition).

2) Escrowed Approval flow
   - Trigger: operator or customer requests a high-risk change or the system heuristics mark a change as high-risk.
   - Escrow window: configurable by customer (default 30m) during which change is staged but not applied by Redwood-managed components. For customer-managed networks, staging means Redwood will not proceed with config-sensitive steps (e.g., routing updates) until escrow cleared.
   - Evidence collection: requestor must attach minimal evidence: config diff, intended timing, rollback plan, and an acceptance signature (OIDC-signed token or HMAC).
   - Approval channels: console button (for named approvers), API call with approver identity, or automated policy (policy-based approvals for low-risk changes).
   - Auto-expiry actions: auto-apply, auto-reject, or auto-escalate to oncall based on customer policy.

3) Evidence bundles
   - Artifact types: text diffs, rendered snapshots of config, verification checksums, pcap pointers (customer S3), metric snapshots (prometheus export), lightweight traceroute captures.
   - Storage model: prefer customer-owned storage (S3 w/ retention policy) for private artifacts. Redwood stores cryptographic manifest and small proof objects in control plane. For customers lacking external storage, Redwood can offer encrypted vaulting (enterprise add-on).

4) Telemetry & Observability
   - Ledger emits structured events to Console and telemetry pipeline: change.requested, change.escrowed, change.approved, change.applied, change.reverted, change.expired.
   - Token-level cost/latency correlation: link change_id into request traces to detect degraded inference post-change.

API surface (proposed minimal)
- POST /v1/private/change-requests -> returns change_id (payload: target, diff, evidence_refs, risk_level, escrow_policy)
- GET /v1/private/change-requests/{change_id} -> full ledger record
- POST /v1/private/change-requests/{change_id}/approve -> approver identity + signature
- POST /v1/private/change-requests/{change_id}/reject -> reason
- POST /v1/private/change-requests/{change_id}/escalate -> route to oncall or customer-notify
- GET /v1/private/change-requests?resource_id=...&since=... -> query by resource/time

Console UX notes
- Timeline view with compact rows: requester, delta summary, approval state, quick links to artifacts.
- Oncall mode: condensed view that surfaces only active escrow windows and auto-actions.
- Investigator mode: filtered timeline with linked per-request metric snapshots and ability to fetch raw artifacts.

Retention and sampling policy (draft)
- Evidence manifests (small proofs, hashes) retained by Redwood for 7 years by default (enterprise), 90 days for standard.
- Large artifacts (pcap, full config snapshots) remain in customer storage; Redwood keeps short-lived signed pointers (30–90 days).
- Sampling: default to store full artifacts for 100% of high-risk changes, and 5% of low-risk changes (configurable).

Acceptance criteria
- Product: Console timeline surfaces CVL entries, supports query and download of evidence manifests for a given timeframe.
- API: change-request creation and approval endpoints implemented with request/response contract above.
- Security: immutable_hash generation validated by security review; signatures verified; RBAC enforced.
- Ops: basic rollback orchestration hook exists that can be invoked for a change_id to initiate customer or operator rollback procedures.
- E2E: Support case simulated where a network change causes a degraded model endpoint response; team can pull ledger, artifacts, and correlate to traces within 15 minutes.

Rollout plan (phased)
- Phase 0 (experimental): internal Redwood-only CVL with console UI + API, no customer storage integration. (2 sprints)
- Phase 1 (beta customers): customer S3 artifact integration, escrow defaults, basic automation policies (4 sprints)
- Phase 2 (GA): retention tiers, oncall escalation, hardened security review and compliance attestation (6 sprints)

Open questions / risks
- Artifacts storage and legal discovery: who has the right to hold packets or config snapshots long-term? Need legal input on jurisdiction and e-discovery policies.
- Performance: indexing and querying large numbers of ledger entries for large customers — we need a pagination and archival strategy.
- Tamper evidence guarantees: what level of guarantee do customers require? Do we need third-party attestation (certificate transparency-style) or is internal immutable hash enough?
- UX friction: escrow windows could block customer workflows; need clear opt-in and sensible defaults.

Next steps
- Sync w/ SRE and Security to validate hashing/signature approach and compliance boundary (share this doc Wed 11/12).
- Prototype minimal POST/GET API and Console timeline with synthetic change events.
- Schedule 1:1 with 2 beta customers (solutions eng) to validate escrow UX and retention preferences.

Notes to self / followups
- Capture mapping of existing PRDs in this folder to avoid duplicate overlap (cc @Elena).
- Add example ledger JSON in appendix (proto) — TODO.
- Draft UX flows for approver invite email and Slack integration for approvals.

-- end of sketch --
